summary: Audit of environment_contract.py integration state. Module exists and exports all required symbols; all 52 unit tests pass. Integration gap is REAL: the module is never imported or called at the Python level anywhere in src/mac/. It is referenced only in documentation strings inside services.py._build_onboarding_description(). Concrete repair plan produced.

services_py_build_onboarding_description.finding: environment_contract is referenced only inside string literals (instruction text for agents). Lines 868, 870, 876, 884 contain doc-string mentions. There is NO Python-level import of environment_contract and NO call to derive_environment_contract or validate_environment_contract anywhere in the function or module.

task_executor_py.finding: No reference to environment_contract, derive_environment_contract, or validate_environment_contract anywhere in the file. The onboarding code path in repository_contract_section() (lines ~2002-2019) constructs instruction text for agents but makes no runtime calls to the module.

repair_plan.description: The environment contract should be derived and attached to the onboarding task metadata at task-creation time so the executing agent receives a pre-computed contract in task.json rather than having to derive it themselves. Two alternative repair sites exist; Site A is preferred because it runs server-side at onboard time.

sites.rationale: Preferred. Runs derive_environment_contract() + validate_environment_contract() once at the moment services.py.onboard_repository() creates the task, so the resulting contract JSON is stored in task metadata and is available to the agent without any extra derivation step. This gives fail-fast semantics (a fatal preflight failure can abort task creation with a clear error) and makes the agent's job simpler.
sites.call_site_description: After the repository is cloned for analysis (the worktree already exists at this point when called via cmd_project_onboard) but before create_task(), call derive_environment_contract(local_checkout_path) and validate_environment_contract(contract), then embed the resulting dict under metadata['environment_contract']. If preflight.status == 'fail', raise a descriptive error.
sites.import_to_add: from mac.environment_contract import derive_environment_contract, validate_environment_contract, environment_contract_summary
sites.code_change_summary: 1. Add import at top of src/mac/services.py. 2. Inside onboard_repository(), after the local checkout path is known, add: contract = derive_environment_contract(local_checkout_path); contract = validate_environment_contract(contract); metadata['environment_contract'] = contract. 3. Optionally: if contract['preflight']['status'] == 'fail', raise RuntimeError with environment_contract_summary(contract) to give the caller an actionable error before a doomed task is queued.
sites.caveat: onboard_repository() does not currently receive a local path argument — it only has the remote URL. The local checkout is prepared later by worker.py when the task is dispatched. If server-side derivation is impractical, use Site B instead.

sites.rationale: Alternative. Runs derive_environment_contract() inside worker.py after the task-owned worktree has been prepared (git clone/worktree complete). Attaches the contract to the task execution context before handing off to the agent prompt. More complex plumbing but does not require the server to have a local checkout.
sites.function: _prepare_repository_task_worktree (or the caller that attaches runtime metadata after worktree creation)
sites.call_site_description: After the worktree is confirmed ready (git worktree add or K8s clone succeeds), call derive_environment_contract(worktree_dir) and validate_environment_contract(contract), then write the result into the task's runtime metadata dict under key 'environment_contract'. If preflight.status == 'fail', log a warning and surface it in the agent prompt.
sites.import_to_add: from mac.environment_contract import derive_environment_contract, validate_environment_contract, environment_contract_summary
sites.code_change_summary: 1. Add import at top of src/mac/worker.py. 2. After worktree is prepared, add: contract = derive_environment_contract(worktree_dir); contract = validate_environment_contract(contract); runtime_metadata['environment_contract'] = contract. 3. If preflight.status == 'fail', include environment_contract_summary(contract) in the agent task prompt warning section.

sites.rationale: Minimal fix: update the instruction text in _build_onboarding_description() to remain accurate (it already describes calling derive_environment_contract) but add a companion in task_executor.py's repository_contract_section() that, when building the onboarding prompt, invokes derive_environment_contract on the $MAC_TASK_REPO_WORKTREE path and injects the result as structured JSON into the prompt. This keeps derivation agent-side but makes it systematic rather than relying on the agent reading and following prose instructions.
sites.call_site_description: In the onboarding branch (has_checkout is True), derive the contract from the worktree path (available via os.environ.get('MAC_TASK_REPO_WORKTREE') or the task metadata) and embed it as a JSON block in the returned prompt string.
sites.code_change_summary: 1. Add import at top of src/mac/task_executor.py. 2. In repository_contract_section(), when has_checkout is True, read MAC_TASK_REPO_WORKTREE, call derive_environment_contract, validate_environment_contract, and inject result JSON into the returned instruction string.

repair_plan.recommended_action: Implement Site B (worker.py, post-worktree-preparation) because: (a) the worktree already exists at that point so the local path is available; (b) keeps contract derivation close to where the physical checkout is created; (c) allows fail-fast before any agent prompt is issued. Follow with updating _build_onboarding_description() in services.py to note that the contract JSON is pre-attached in task metadata (not requiring the agent to re-derive it).

assumptions: onboard_repository() in services.py does not receive a pre-cloned local path; clone happens later in worker.py — so Site A as described would require refactoring; Site B is more immediately actionable.
No code changes were made; this is a pure investigation deliverable as specified.
